reason: QAC-style resources can split إذ from يومئذ; this is a lemma-boundary convention, not a proven error. Preserve until token-segmentation model is globally redesigned.
The same written lemma functions as relative/interrogative nominal forms and as negative/other particles; mixed N/P is linguistically motivated.
QAC treats إذا as a time adverb in many contexts; PureMonotheism coarse schema does not have a dedicated T tag, so N/P mapping is schema-dependent.
Temporal/subordinating and negative uses differ; collapsing to one POS would erase grammatical distinctions.
نَعَم 'yes' is a particle, while root-related nominal/verbal forms belong to separate lexical analyses.
Independent QAC analysis treats it as a nominative masculine noun/elative 'best calculated', so minority N is not an error.
Independent morphology treats participles as derived nominals even when semantically verbal.
70:16 الشوى is a noun 'skin/scalp' while the verbal homograph is distinct; POS divergence is legitimate.
